device.description: 8-bit 1.5 us half-flash microprocessor-compatible ADC with track/hold and 3-state data bus
device.note: adc0820-n.pdf (SNAS529C) p.2 operating ratings, p.4 DC characteristics (logic levels), p.5 AC characteristics (tI, tACC2, t1H/t0H, tINTH), p.6-7 Figures 4-7 (RD mode, WR-RD mode timing), p.10 pin descriptions (WR/RDY, Mode, RD, INT, OFL)

commands.name: Start conversion (WR-RD mode: CS and WR low)

pages: p.2 (operating ratings: VCC 4.5-8 V), p.4 (VIN(1) 2.0 V CS/WR/RD, 3.5 V Mode), p.5 (tCRD 2.5 us, tI 800/1300 ns, tACC2 120/150 ns, t1H/t0H 200 ns, tINTH 225 ns, tRDY 100 ns), p.6-7 (Figures 4-7), p.10 (pin descriptions)
notModeled: analog input, VREF(+)/VREF(-) span (the result is always the 0 V code 0x00)
only WR-RD mode (MODE pin high) is modeled: WR/RDY is the WR input, the conversion is started by CS+WR and INT goes low tI (1300 ns max) after WR rises. The MODE pin is not read

RD mode (MODE low, the power-on default: MODE has an internal 50 uA pull-down): RD low starts the conversion and the data appear on DB0-DB7 at its end (tCRD 2.5 us max) in the same read; pin 6 is then RDY, an open-drain output low from CS fall until the result is latched
WR-RD mode reading before tI (RD low earlier latches the result at RD fall, INT low tRD+290 ns)
INT is also reset by the rising edge of CS; INT state at power-up is undefined
OFL overflow output (always driven, low when VIN > VREF(+); high for the 0 V code) is not driven
conversion starts at the WR falling edge in the datasheet; the model starts it at WR/CS release and times tI from there (which is how the datasheet times INT)
tWR / tRD minimum (600 ns) and maximum (50 us) widths, tP 500 ns between conversions
pin names: VREF(−) is written VREF(-); Mode is written MODE
variants: ADC0820BCWM / ADC0820CCWM differ only in accuracy grade (+-1/2 vs +-1 LSB); one device
